rows.Bloom: Orange blend. Orange with white markings and white reverse. Mild fragrance. 30 to 35 petals. Average diameter 4". Medium, full (26-40 petals), borne mostly solitary, in small clusters bloom form.
rows.Habit:
Medium, bushy. Medium, semi-glossy, medium green foliage.

Height: 3' to 4' (90 to 120cm).
rows.Breeder's notes:
Prickles: medium , triangular base, downward pointing, brown;
young foliage tinted bronze.

This is one of our best of our ‘hand-painted’ roses, the fascinating ever-changing combinations of bright orange, pastel vermillion and white, which so distinguishes this rose, making it most eye-catching. We have bred this rose many years ago, but had not released it. When we visited the USA in June 2013, we went on a marvelous road trip from Washington DC all the way down to Boynton Beach and Lakeland in Miami, with our good friend Gene Waering at the wheel. Two days into our trip, Pat Shanley, presently Vice president, but the incoming president of the American Rose Society joined us , and we had a wonderful time together. Pat is a dear friend whom we have known since 2005, when we were her ( and her late husband John’s) house guests in their beautiful house on Long Island. Viru was a speaker at the Manhattan Rose Society, of which she was ( and continues to be) President , and she threw a lovely party for us. On this present trip , when she saw Viru’s roses being grown in many gardens , and also saw his PPT lecture at Jacksonville where she saw the many other roses he has bred, she was enchanted and most appreciative. We felt we would like to reciprocate her friendliness, affection and warmth, by naming a rose for her, and when we showed her the photograph of this hand-painted rose, she was delighted and agreed to have it named for her. We are delighted too.
2013 A new grandiflora rose in the hand painted strain with flowers of exquisite form of white with salmon orange stripes and blotches. Every flower is a different mix of colors adding to the distinctive beauty of this rose.
rows.Parentage:
Sonia (hybrid tea, Meilland, 1973) ×
Maestro ® (hybrid tea, McGredy, 1972)
rows.Notes: A 'hand-painted' variety, which has Picasso in its lineage.
